Gaza
The mathematics of starvation: how Israel caused a famine in Gaza
Israel controls the flow of food into Gaza. It has calculated how many calories Palestinians need to stay alive. Its data shows only a fraction has been allowed in
Emma Graham-Harrison
Chief Middle East correspondent
Thu 31 Jul 2025 10.49 EDT
Last modified on Thu 31 Jul 2025 16.02 EDT
Share
T
he mathematics of famine are simple in Gaza. Palestinians cannot leave, war has ended farming and
Israel
has banned fishing, so practically every calorie its population eats must be brought in from outside.
Israel knows how much food is needed. It has been calibrating hunger in
Gaza
for decades, initially calculating shipments to exert pressure while avoiding starvation.
Children and elderly people most vulnerable as Gaza famine deepens, warn experts
Read more
“The idea is to put the Palestinians on a diet, but not to make them die of hunger,” a senior adviser to the then prime minister, Ehud Olmert,
said
in 2006. An Israeli court ordered the release of documents showing the
details
of those macabre sums two years later.
Cogat, the Israeli agency that still controls aid shipments to Gaza, calculated then that Palestinians needed an average minimum 2,279 calories per person per day, which could be provided through 1.836kg of food.
Today, humanitarian organisations are asking for an even smaller minimum ration: 62,000 metric tonnes of dry and canned food to meet basic needs for 2.1 million people each month, or around 1kg of food per person per day.
As Gaza has slid into famine this summer, Israeli officials have variously
denied
the existence of mass starvation, claimed
without
evidence
that Hamas steals and hoards aid, or blamed hunger on UN distribution failures, sharing pictures of aid pallets awaiting collection inside the border.
bar chart showing that more people in Gaza died of starvation in just over 11 days than in the previous 21 months of conflict
They pointed to
deadly and chaotic
food distributions by the Gaza Humanitarian Foundation, a US and Israeli-backed logistics startup, as proof that Palestinians had access to food.
Yet data compiled and published by Israel’s own government makes clear that it has been starving Gaza. Between March and June, Israel allowed just 56,000 tonnes of food to enter the territory, Cogat records show, less than a quarter of Gaza’s minimum needs for that period.
How will the UK’s recognition of Palestine help those starving in Gaza? - podcast
Read more
Even if every bag of UN flour had been collected and handed out, and the GHF had developed safe systems for equitable distribution, starvation was inevitable. Palestinians did not have enough to eat.
A “worst-case scenario” famine is now unfolding in Gaza, UN-backed food security experts said this week. Food deliveries are “at a scale far below what is needed”, amid “drastic restrictions on the entry of supplies”, the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) said in a report citing Israeli figures on aid.
The
Famine
Review Committee, an independent group of experts that scrutinises IPC alerts, said food shipments “have been highly inadequate”, and singled out the GHF.
“Our analysis of the food packages supplied by the GHF shows that their distribution plan would lead to mass starvation, even if it was able to function without the appalling levels of violence that have been reported,” the FRC said.
In March and April Gaza was under total siege, with no food entering. In mid-May Netanyahu said shipments would restart because of international pressure over a “starvation crisis”.
View image in fullscreen
Data compiled and published by Israel’s own government makes clear that it has been starving Gaza.
Photograph: Anadolu/Getty Images
Just a few weeks of extra aid shipments during the ceasefire in January and February this year provided enough calories to bring Gaza back from the brink of famine, UN data shows.
However, in May only a trickle of food returned, in quantities that served only to slow Gaza’s descent into starvation, not stop it. Two months on, the scale of suffering has now spurred another round of international outrage, including
demands
from Donald Trump to get “every ounce of food” to starving children.
chart showing that by Israel’s own figures, the amount of aid reaching Gaza falls well below subsistence levels
In response Netanyahu has promised only “minimal” extra aid. The number of food trucks entering the territory has risen, but is still well below the minimum needed to feed Palestinians there, much less reverse a famine.
View image in fullscreen
Aid packages, dropped from a plane, descend into Gaza.
Photograph: Hatem Khaled/Reuters

主要讨论点：AI本地优先的会议笔记软件的发布及相关技术、商业模式、功能和用户体验讨论

不同观点：
• **itsalotoffun**：对项目发布时列出的大公司客户名单表示怀疑，认为这些公司是通过多年艰苦的销售努力才获得的，而非通过一次发布。
• **yonl**：赞赏软件的本地优先和开源性质，分享自己使用类似自建解决方案的经验，并对API和钩子的开放表示期待。
• **teiferer**：祝贺发布，但希望了解项目的 monetization 计划，特别是考虑到与YC的关系，关注是否会有隐性成本。
• **polyaniline**：尝试在Linux上构建软件时遇到需要多个API密钥的问题，认为这不符合本地优先软件的预期。
• **jihomie**：作为一名技术公司的经理，对软件在合规性和自托管方面的能力感兴趣，希望了解如何在个人设备上实现并说服合规团队。
• **crashabr**：关注软件是否能达到MacWhisper的功能水平，特别是自动会议检测和自定义转录操作，并对发言者检测功能提出改进建议。
• **btown**：关心实时转录的准确性与时间延迟的平衡问题，希望能够自定义这种平衡以适应不同的使用场景。

补充讨论：
• **mentalgear**：对开源和本地优先表示赞赏，但好奇项目的商业模式，特别是如何在不依赖技术用户的情况下产生收入。
• **whitefang**：分享了自己构建类似项目的经验，强调完全开源和无需API调用的特点，认为模型质量可以通过新模型得到改善。
• **ljosa**：在实际使用中发现缺乏发言者区分功能是重大缺陷，认为这对于多人会议非常重要。
• **p2hari**：在Mac M4 pro mini上遇到启动失败问题，给予权限后仍无法解决，寻求帮助。
• **theodorewiles**：对企业级智能同意管理功能表示关注，讨论了法律合规性和用户体验之间的平衡。
• **AlexErrant**：作为语音控制应用的开发者，关注软件的回声消除功能，特别是平台特定的非ML技术API的使用经验。
• **nashashmi**：分享了使用AI笔记功能制作教程的实际案例，展示了软件的实际应用场景。
• **rushingcreek**：对软件的本地运行能力和低参数模型的使用表示赞赏，并提出通过模型更新和LoRA技术提升用户体验的建议。

争议焦点：
• 软件是否真正实现了本地优先，特别是在需要多个API密钥和遇到构建问题的情况下。
• 开源软件如何在保持免费的同时产生收入，用户对潜在商业模式的接受度。
• 实时转录功能的准确性与延迟之间的平衡，特别是对于不同使用场景的需求。
• 软件在多人会议中的实用性，特别是发言者区分功能的缺失。

data.title: Sweeney confirms Epic Games Store launch on Play Store after Google loses appeal
data.author: bundie
data.article_summary: 谷歌在与Epic Games的法律纠纷中上诉失败，法院维持原判，要求谷歌开放Play商店。2023年12月的审判认定谷歌通过其Play商店和支付系统非法垄断，强制对开发者收取15%到30%的佣金。法院命令谷歌允许用户从Play商店下载竞争对手的应用商店，允许开发者使用自己的支付系统，并不得阻止开发者告知用户外部更便宜的购买选项。谷歌对该命令提出上诉，但上诉法院驳回其请求。Epic Games CEO对结果表示庆祝，而谷歌则担忧此决定会影响用户安全和Android生态系统的创新，并可能向美国最高法院提起上诉。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对Tim Sweeney（Epic Games CEO）的评价和其公司商业行为的讨论

不同观点：
• 正面评价：一些用户认为Tim Sweeney是行业的变革者，特别是在对抗苹果公司垄断行为的过程中表现出色。他推动了游戏行业对垄断行为的挑战，并为开发者争取了更多的利益。有评论提到，Sweeney对开放平台和自由市场的倡导为其他公司树立了榜样，尤其是他通过Epic Games与苹果的对抗，挑战了应用商店的高额抽成制度。

• 负面评价：另一部分用户对Tim Sweeney持批评态度，认为他只是在维护Epic Games自身的利益，而不是真正关心开发者或行业的整体发展。有人指出，Epic Games自己的游戏平台和商业模式也存在一定的封闭性和垄断嫌疑，因此认为Sweeney的行为是出于自身利益，而非纯粹的行业改革。

• 对商业模式的讨论：有评论指出，Epic Games通过《Fortnite》等游戏积累了大量财富，并通过这些资源来支持其与苹果等大公司的法律对抗。批评者认为，Epic Games的这种做法实际上是在利用其游戏成功后的资源进行商业斗争，而不是真正为了开放市场。支持者则认为，利用自身资源进行法律对抗是合理的，因为这有助于推动整个行业的变革。

• 对行业影响的讨论：一部分评论认为，Epic Games与苹果的对抗有可能改变整个科技行业的商业模式，特别是在应用商店抽成和平台封闭性方面。支持者认为，这种对抗可能会促使其他平台进行改革，从而为开发者和消费者带来更多选择和利益。批评者则担心，这种对抗可能会导致行业的不稳定，甚至引发更多的法律和商业纠纷。

补充讨论：
• 一些评论还提到了Epic Games在游戏行业中的其他行为，比如其虚幻引擎（Unreal Engine）对开发者的影响。支持者认为，虚幻引擎为许多开发者提供了强大的工具，推动了行业的技术进步。批评者则认为，Epic Games通过虚幻引擎和其他商业手段，也在建立自己的生态系统，可能导致新的封闭和垄断。

• 关于法律对抗的结果，一些评论表示关注。他们认为，无论结果如何，这种法律对抗可能会持续很长时间，并对整个行业产生深远影响。支持者希望这能带来积极的变化，而批评者则担心这可能会带来更多的不确定性和风险。

争议的焦点：Tim Sweeney及其公司Epic Games的行为是否真正为了推动行业改革和开放市场，还是仅仅为了自身利益。

44749202.article_content:
In the San Francisco-based 9th Circuit Court of Appeals today, Google faced its ongoing legal fight with Epic Games, where, unfortunately for the company, it lost its appeal against a federal court order that demanded it open up the Play Store.
This decision
upholds the conclusion of the original trial with Epic Games in December 2023, which delivered a huge victory for the
Fortnite
maker after a jury found that Google maintained an illegal monopoly with its Google Play store and Google Play Billing service.
The core of Epic's argument was that Google actively suppressed competition by tying its store to its payment system, effectively forcing a 15 to 30% commission on developers. The jury agreed. The company's legal team had presented evidence of Google paying off other developers to keep them from launching their own app stores, which did not help its case at all.
The real pain for Google came in October last year, when Judge James Donato ordered the Mountain View giant to open things up. Google was told to do the following, among other things:
Allow users to download rival app stores from within the Play Store.
Permit developers to use their own billing systems for in-app purchases.
Stop preventing developers from telling users about cheaper purchasing options outside the app.
Google, hating every part of that order,
filed its appeal a month later in November
, hoping to get it thrown out.
There is a difference in the way both companies reacted to today's news. Tim Sweeney, Epic Games CEO, was (obviously) celebratory on X, claiming that thanks to the verdict, the Epic Games Store for Android will be "coming to the Google Play Store."
Thanks to the verdict, the Epic Games Store for Android will be coming to the Google Play Store! It's already available worldwide from our web site,
https://t.co/f77ZSrBMGd
.
Epic Games Store for PC already carries several other PC stores (
https://t.co/92elnB3IGv
, GOG Galaxy).
https://t.co/4ndkMmhLUX
— Tim Sweeney (@TimSweeneyEpic)
July 31, 2025
On the other hand, Google's VP of regulatory affairs, Lee-Anne Mulholland, stated that the ruling "will significantly harm user safety, limit choice, and undermine the innovation that has always been central to the Android ecosystem", adding that Google will continue its appeal.
Google's defense during the appeal process hinged on arguments that it faces stiff competition from Apple and that the court's orders would compromise Android's security. Now, with the appeals court not convinced, Google is running out of options; its last resort is an appeal to the U.S. Supreme Court.

争议的焦点：Tim Sweeney及其公司Epic Games的行为是否真正为了推动行业改革和开放市场，还是仅仅为了自身利益。

data.article_summary: 文章简要回顾了数据交换格式的发展，重点介绍了三种格式：XML、JSON和CBOR。XML源于20世纪60-70年代IBM的GML，后来演变为SGML，并于1996年通过W3C简化为XML，旨在为互联网提供结构化的数据交换格式。XML具有良好的可扩展性和兼容性，但较为冗长。JSON则是为Web应用设计的轻量级格式，语法简单，更注重性能和易用性。CBOR是针对物联网等资源受限环境设计的二进制格式，强调高效和紧凑。每种格式都在特定历史背景下解决了不同的技术需求，反映了数据交换格式不断演变的趋势。

主要讨论点：CBOR数据格式及其与其他数据格式（如JSON、XML、MessagePack等）的比较

不同观点：
• **CBOR的定位和重要性**：
  - **mrbluecoat**：认为将CBOR称为“关键数据格式”言过其实，与其他格式如Protobuf、Parquet、Avro和Cap'n Proto相比，CBOR并非那么重要。
  - **nabla9**：认为CBOR在需要非常小的代码体积时具有优势，但在可以使用压缩的情况下，CBOR相对于JSON没有显著的数据体积优势。

• **CBOR与JSON的对比**：
  - **_the_inflator**：赞赏JSON的简洁和易用性，尽管需要为datetime、BLOBs等写类型转换器，但这些转换器正是JSON实用性的原因。此外，JSON的灵活性使其在简单和复杂需求之间取得平衡。
  - **brookst**：指出文章中缺少CBOR的具体示例，使其难以理解CBOR的具体表现形式。

• **CBOR与其他二进制格式的对比**：
  - **makapuf**：认为ASN.1在简洁性和通用性上优于CBOR等格式。
  - **camgunz**：认为CBOR和MessagePack在本质上是相同的，但CBOR的标签注册机制和标准化的扩展类型并不实用，且增加了解码负担。

• **CBOR的实际应用**：
  - **JoelJacobson**：提到CBOR在WebAuthn（Passkey）协议中的实际应用，并分享了一个纯SQL/PLpgSQL CBOR解析器的实现。
  - **gethly**：希望浏览器能原生支持CBOR，以便在提高速度的同时减少数据体积，而不需要担心解码问题。

• **CBOR的细节和技术问题**：
  - **aidenn0**：对CBOR浮点数表示的准确性提出疑问，并指出文档中的潜在错误。
  - **fjfaase**：提到文档的下一部分将CBOR与其他二进制存储格式（如protobuf）进行比较。

• **CBOR的历史和社区讨论**：
  - **dang**：提供了一些与CBOR相关的历史讨论链接，显示出社区对CBOR和MessagePack的长期争论。
  - **JimDabell**：提到之前关于CBOR和MessagePack选择的讨论。

• **ASN.1的实际应用**：
  - **johnisgood**：分享了Erlang/Elixir对ASN.1的良好支持，并对比了Java/Kotlin在ASN.1支持上的不足。

补充讨论：
• **压缩与格式比较**：
  - **glenjamin**：指出文档中对压缩的提及不足，并建议比较压缩后的JSON和CBOR，以获得更全面的理解。

• **对CBOR的幽默批评**：
  - **naggumsghost**：以幽默的方式批评CBOR，并引用了一个对XML的激烈批评，暗示需要为CBOR想出一个类似的“激烈批评”。

争议焦点：
• CBOR是否真的如宣传所言是“关键数据格式”，以及其相对于其他格式（如JSON、MessagePack、ASN.1等）的实际优势和应用场景。

44732593.article_content:
From XML to JSON to CBOR A Lingua Franca for Data? In modern computing, data exchange is foundational to everything from web browsing to microservices and IoT devices. The ability for different systems to represent, share, and interpret structured information drives our digital world. Yet no single perfect format has emerged to meet all needs. Instead, we've seen an evolution of data interchange formats, each addressing the specific challenges and technical requirements of its time. This narrative traces three pivotal data formats: Extensible Markup Language ( XML ), JavaScript Object Notation ( JSON ), and Concise Binary Object Representation ( CBOR ). We explore their origins and motivations, examine their core design principles and inherent trade-offs, and follow their adoption trajectories within the evolving digital landscape. The journey begins with XML's focus on robust document structure, shifts to JSON's web-centric simplicity and performance, and advances to CBOR's binary efficiency for constrained devices. Understanding this evolution reveals not just technical specifications, but the underlying pressures driving innovation in data interchange formats. The Age of Structure: XML's Rise from Publishing Roots Modern data interchange formats trace back not to the web, but to challenges in electronic publishing decades earlier. SGML provided the complex foundation that XML would later refine and adapt for the internet age. The SGML Inheritance: Laying the Foundation In the 1960s-70s, IBM researchers Charles Goldfarb, Ed Mosher, and Ray Lorie created Generalized Markup Language (GML) to overcome proprietary typesetting limitations. Their approach prioritized content structure over presentation. GML later evolved into Standard Generalized Markup Language (SGML), formalized as ISO 8879 in 1986. SGML innovated through its meta-language approach, providing rules for creating custom markup languages. It allowed developers to define specific vocabularies (tag sets) and grammars (Document Type Definitions or DTDs) for different document types, creating machine-readable documents with exceptional longevity independent of processing technologies. SGML gained traction in sectors managing complex documentation: government, military (CALS DTD), aerospace, legal publishing, and heavy industry. However, its 150+ page specification with numerous special cases complicated parser implementation, limiting broader adoption. The web's emergence proved pivotal for markup languages. Tim Berners-Lee selected SGML as HTML's foundation due to its text-based, flexible, non-proprietary nature. Dan Connolly created the first HTML DTD in 1992. While HTML became ubiquitous, it drifted toward presentation over structure, with proliferating browser-specific extensions. SGML remained too complex for widespread web use, creating demand for a format that could bring SGML's structural capabilities to the internet in a more accessible form. W3C and the Birth of XML: Taming SGML for the Web By the mid-1990s, the web needed more structured data exchange beyond HTML's presentational focus. In 1996, the W3C established an XML Working Group, chaired by Jon Bosak of Sun Microsystems, to create a simplified SGML subset suitable for internet use while maintaining extensibility and structure. The W3C XML Working Group developed XML with clear design goals, formalized in the XML 1 Specification (W3C Recommendation, February 1998): Internet Usability : Straightforward use over the internet Broad Applicability : Support for diverse applications beyond browsers SGML Compatibility : XML documents should be conforming SGML documents Ease of Processing : Simple program development for XML processing Minimal Optional Features : Few or no optional features Human Readability : Legible and clear documents Rapid Design : Quick design process Formal and Concise Design : Formal specification amenable to standard parsing Ease of Creation : Simple document creation with basic tools Terseness is Minimally Important : Conciseness was not prioritized over clarity SGML compatibility was strategically crucial. By defining XML as a valid SGML subset, existing SGML parsers and tools could immediately process XML documents when the standard released in 1998. This lowered adoption barriers for organizations already using SGML and provided an instant software ecosystem. The constraint also helped the working group achieve rapid development by limiting design choices, demonstrating an effective strategy for launching the new standard. Designing XML: Tags, Attributes, Namespaces, and Schemas XML's structure uses nested elements marked by tags.
